pr_title: samples: blinky_pwm: decreased min PWM period for blinky sample
pr_body:
Blinky PWM sample minimum pwm period was too high for iMX.RT PWM module.
decrease the minimum pwm period so sample will pass pwm calibration
phase, and successfully run

Fixes #38954

Signed-off-by: Daniel DeGrasse <daniel.degrasse@nxp.com>

@ric96 I'm assuming you're using an external pin and LED for the teensy board, as the onboard LED is routed to `GPIO_B0_03`, which does not have a MUX option for the PWM module:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/34665051/153059113-e4cbe0ba-c495-436a-81c6-f3ca8f424ed1.png)
In that case, you will need to add a function call to `IOMUXC_SetPinConfig` to select the correct flexPWM module, based on what you define in your dts overlay.

Regardless of your specific setup for PWM on the teensy, the blinky PWM sample does not work on RT series SOCs (I reproduced the issue on an RT1064 EVK), because the pwm sample does not attempt to calibrate PWM with a short enough period. The RT series flexPWM module's source clock is too fast to support PWM at any frequency lower than roughly 18 Hz, and the blinky sample never tries to set up PWM with a frequency that is this high. The linked pull request increases the maximum frequency the sample will try to use from 16 Hz to 32 Hz, allowing it to run.
